long_biography.plain_text:
Carlo Adolfo Rivetti was born in Lausanne and studied economics at Bocconi University before entering Gruppo Finanziario Tessile, the apparel group controlled by his family. He eventually ran its sportswear division, where the Stone Island label grew from Massimo Osti's experiments with technical fabrics and garment dyeing. Rivetti and his sister Cristina acquired the Ravarino operation in 1993 and renamed it Sportswear Company.

Rivetti narrowed the business around Stone Island, selling C.P. Company and taking over creative direction. He expanded distribution and collaborations while preserving the brand's material research and utilitarian design language. The Rivetti family brought in Temasek as a minority investor, then sold its controlling interest to Moncler. Rivetti remained chairman after the transaction but had left both Stone Island's chairmanship and Moncler's board by 2026.
